newsitem.title: USA: Italy making big effort to curb deficit - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy making big effort to curb deficit - Fazio.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Tuesday Italy was making strenuous efforts to curb its state deficit, and that progress so far had freed domestic resources for investments abroad.
"Italy is presently engaged in a strenuous effort to reduce its budget deficit and the public debt to GDP ratio," Fazio said at a meeting of the International Monetary Fund Development Committee.

"Fiscal consolidation has greatly reduced the pressure of the government's borrowing requirements on domestic savings, thereby freeing a growing portion of Italian domestic resources for investments abroad," Fazio said.

Italy is striving to reach a 3.0 pct deficit-to-GDP ratio by the end of 1997, down from 6.7 pct in 1996, in order to meet requirements to participate in the first wave of countries entering the European single currency system.

The IMF forecasts Italy will miss the target narrowly, reducing the deficit/GDP ratio to 3.3 pct by year-end, while the European Commission indicates a 3.2 pct ratio, but adds that if all the budget-cutting measures enacted so far take full effect, the 3.0 pct goal is within reach.

Fazio said probably the most important contribution indiviual countries can provide to international cooperation was to adopt sound domestic policies, which, in the richest countries, should be aimed at low budget deficits and no inflation in order to accelerate trade and growth.
Italy believes the declining trend in foreign aid "should be arrested" and seeks a clear improvement in aid effectiveness, Fazio said.
The World Bank "should redouble its efforts to diversify its approaches to development assistance," Fazio said.

Welcoming progress by the World Bank and the IMF in implementing a debt relief initiative for poor countries, Fazio said total financing of the initiative should be firmly established, and the beneficiaries clearly defined.
